chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you stand in the two rak'ahs of the Dhuhr prayer or others, and you did not recite the Tashahhud in them, and you remembered that in the third rak'ah before you bow (for ruku'), then sit and recite the Tashahhud, then stand and complete your prayer. And if you did not remember until you bow, then proceed in your prayer until you finish. When you have finished, prostrate the two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sujadat al-Sahw) after the Taslim, before you speak."
ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for correcting a missed Tashahhud in prayer based on when it is remembered?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural mechanics of *Sujadat al-Sahw* (prostrations of forgetfulness) specifically regarding the omission of the *Tashahhud* in the first two rak'ahs. It establishes a critical jurisprudential distinction: if remembered before *ruku'* (bowing), the worshipper returns to complete the omission; if remembered after *ruku'*, the prayer is completed and the prostrations are performed after the final *taslim*. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precision in prayer structure while accommodating human error without invalidating the act of worship.
